49/G.goal: Explain how VR experience optimization is guided by cybersickness and presence constraints, from the trade-off with resource utilization through locomotion choices to the need for walking-speed-matched optic flow in system-controlled tours.
49/G.achieves: This supports the course aim of addressing psycho-physiological issues and optimization from user and developer perspectives, preparing the learner to understand and evaluate immersive XR experience design.

49/O1.goal: Explain why immersive VR optimization should prioritize psychophysiological experience over technological resource utilization by identifying cybersickness causes and the presence constraints on mitigation.
49/O1.achieves: This helps the learner understand the user-centric aim of VR optimization and the comfort and presence constraints that mitigation strategies must satisfy.

49/O2.goal: Describe how VR locomotion and user- and system-controlled tour choices can reduce cybersickness through shorter navigation duration or distance, and why system-controlled tours require realistic walking with optic flow matched to the user's instantaneous speed.
49/O2.achieves: This lets the learner identify the movement-design problem in VR tours and understand why a walking-speed model is needed to keep optic flow realistic and comfortable.
